- When sentiment is predominantly negative (-1.00) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast upward moves; correct by adding 2–5% to forecast if true outcome exceeds prior 3–5 day high.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day average), model often over-estimates continuation; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., -1.00 → 1.00), model frequently under-reacts; increase forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days if sentiment remains positive.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–3% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often under-predicts late-period (last 7–10 days) true values; adjust forecast by +1–3% for final 7 days if sentiment remains negative.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (1.00) and price is trending up, model may over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 3–5 days if true outcome shows deceleration.
